sections.label: Waste management PWM accepted
sections.summary: The Government accepted TCWM recommendations to introduce a Progressive Wage Model for waste collection and materials recovery sub-sectors comprising around 550 firms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: In January last year, the Government accepted the Tripartite Cluster for Waste Management (TCWM)'s recommendations to introduce a Progressive Wage Model (PWM) for the waste collection and materials recovery sub-sectors, which currently comprise around 550 firms.

sections.label: Waste collection crew baseline wage
sections.summary: The entry-level baseline wage for waste collection crew grows 8.1% annually from $2,210 per month in 2023 to $3,260 per month in 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: For instance, the entry-level baseline wage for waste collection crew will grow by 8.1% annually from $2,210 per month in 2023 to $3,260 per month in 2028.

sections.label: Cleaning sector licensing regime
sections.summary: The cleaning sector has around 1,530 licensed businesses and 53,600 cleaners, and a licensing regime was introduced in September 2014 mandating PWM wages and training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The cleaning sector comprises around 1,530 licensed cleaning businesses, with a total workforce of about 53,600 cleaners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Subsequently, a licensing regime was introduced in September 2014 to mandate the minimum requirements for cleaning businesses, including the payment of PWM wages and the requisite training for cleaners.

sections.label: Revised cleaning licence classes
sections.summary: The revised framework will have three licence classes differentiating cleaning businesses by capabilities, unlike the current regime granting the same licence to all.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The revised framework will comprise three classes of licences to differentiate cleaning businesses according to their capabilities, as opposed to the current licensing regime, which grants the same licence to all cleaning businesses as long as they fulfil a set of common licensing requirements.

sections.label: Minimum paid-up capital requirement
sections.summary: The minimum paid-up capital or net worth of $25,000 ensures cleaning businesses are committed and able to pay PWM wages to cleaners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The minimum paid-up capital or net worth of $25,000 ensures that the cleaning businesses are committed and able to pay PWM wages to their cleaners.

sections.label: Class 1 licence requirements
sections.summary: The Class 1 licence requires a higher minimum paid-up capital or net worth of $250,000 and additional WSQ training for the cleaning workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The Class 1 licence requires licensees to meet a higher minimum paid-up capital or net worth of $250,000 and to ensure that their cleaning workforce is trained in additional Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) modules.

sections.label: High-rise littering feedback increase
sections.summary: Feedback on high-rise littering rose from an average of 19,000 cases in 2017-2019 to 31,200 in 2020-2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Feedback on high-rise littering has increased by over 60% between two consecutive three-year periods, from an average of 19,000 cases between 2017 and 2019, to an average of 31,200 cases between 2020 and 2022.

sections.label: Presumption for flat littering
sections.summary: A new Section 17A creates rebuttable presumptions that owners or tenants who leased the whole flat committed the littering offence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The Bill will insert a new Section 17A to introduce rebuttable presumptions such that if there is clear evidence that a littering act has been committed from a residential flat the owners or tenants who have leased the whole residential flat, will be presumed to have committed the littering offence.

sections.label: Waste disposal and limitation period
sections.summary: The Bill amends Section 20 to make causing or permitting illegal waste disposal an offence and Section 95 to extend the limitation period from one to three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The Bill will amend Section 20 to make it an offence to cause or permit such illegal disposal of waste.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The amendment will enable enforcement action to be taken against supervisors and not just the workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: Another amendment relates to the one-year limitation period which prevents NEA from prosecuting an accused person for offences committed under the EPHA unless it is within one year from the date of offence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: There have been instances where NEA had been unable to enforce against an accused person within the one-year limitation period.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: The Bill will thus amend Section 95 to extend the limitation period mentioned in that section from one year to three years to allow NEA more time to investigate complex cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: However, the time bar does not apply if, by reason of the offence complained of, an injury or danger to health subsists at the date of the complaint.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
sentences.text: This Bill represents another milestone in our journey towards safeguarding public health and maintaining high standards of public cleanliness that Singapore is known for.

sections.label: Conditions on progressive wages
sections.summary: New section 23A introduces powers to impose conditions on payment of progressive wages to Singaporean and PR waste disposal workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 23A introduces powers to impose conditions on the payment of progressive wages to Singaporean and permanent resident (PR) holder waste disposal workers.

sections.label: Class 1 licence requirements
sections.summary: A Class 1 licence requires businesses to have $250,000 paid-up capital and no conviction history in the past 24 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A Class 1 licence will require businesses to have a paid-up capital of $250,000 and a clean record with no conviction history in the past 24 months.

sections.label: Extending presumption to smoking
sections.summary: The proposal extends the high-rise littering presumption to smoking in flats, with new section 17A presuming every owner or tenant threw the litter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What I propose we do is extend the presumption introduced for high-rise littering to smoking in flats that affect other residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 17A will introduce a presumption clause that the litter proven to be thrown from a flat was thrown by every owner or tenant of the flat.

sections.label: Tham letter on littering presumption
sections.summary: Ms Tham wrote to Senior Minister of State Amy Khor, copying the speaker, about the statutory presumption clause for high-rise littering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On 10 January, Ms Tham wrote to Senior Minister of State Amy Khor and copied me in the email.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: She shared, "I was delighted to read about the statutory presumption clause for high-rise littering, aimed to place greater onus on flat owners and tenants to prevent littering.

sections.label: Tham's upstairs neighbour smoking
sections.summary: Ms Tham shared her story of an upstairs neighbour who smokes several times a day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To be honest, merely making it illegal would be a great help, plus the suggestion that surveillance might catch them in the act." "This is my story" – that Ms Tham shared: "I have an upstairs neighbour who smokes several times a day.

sections.label: Neighbour refused smoking timing requests
sections.summary: The neighbour refused requests to smoke at designated times, and he and his landlord said smoking on the balcony is not illegal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We’ve asked him to alert us in advance when he is about to smoke, or smoke at designated times so that we can close our windows and doors in advance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, he refused to do so and the response we got from him and his landlord was that 'it is not illegal' for him to smoke in the balcony." "My father-in-law passed away in 2021 from nose cancer, despite not being a smoker.

sections.label: Call to study second-hand smoke
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Ministry will study the issue further and consider a similar presumption clause for second-hand smoke in flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Her story is one that would be familiar to many Singaporeans and Members of this house.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I know I sound like a broken record but I hope the Ministry will study this issue much further and consider whether a similar presumption clause may help to address the problem of second-hand smoke in flats.

sections.label: Clause 17A litter presumption
sections.summary: Clause 17A makes owners or tenants responsible for litter from their flat landing in a public place, with a rebuttable presumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this Bill, the new Clause 17A holds the owner or tenant to be responsible for litter emanating from any flat that lands in a "public place".

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Ministry's press release states and I quote: "The presumption can be rebutted by the owner/tenant by proving that he/she was not present in the flat at the time of the offence, by proving that he/she could not have been the offender, or by providing the identity of a person reasonably believed to be the offender to NEA within 14 days of being required to do so." The effect of the presumption is that unless rebutted, it presumes that the owner or tenant is the offender and thus makes the owner or tenant liable for the acts of the offender, if the owner and offender are different people.

sections.label: Standard of proof clarification
sections.summary: The speaker asks what standard of proof an owner must meet to rebut the presumption of guilt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My first clarification is, what is the standard of proof that needs to be met by the owner to rebut the presumption of guilt?

sections.label: Rebuttable presumption of guilt grounds
sections.summary: Section 17A(5) allows the presumption of guilt to be rebutted by proving another person's contravention, absence from the flat, or reasonable belief with identity provided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Section 17A(5) provides that the presumption of guilt is rebuttable by proving any of these: (a) contravention committed by person other than presumed offender; (b) presumed offender not in flat at time of offence; (c) presumed offender reasonably believing someone else is the actual offender and providing the identity of that person.

sections.label: NEA FAQ on elderly disabled
sections.summary: NEA's FAQ on the new Bill asked whether the legislation would apply to elderly or mentally or physically disabled home owners or tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the NEA's Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) section on the new Bill, it was stated and I quote, "Will the new legislation be applicable to home owners/tenants who are elderly or mentally/physically disabled?

sections.label: NEA review and appeals concerns
sections.summary: NEA reviews each case before action, and the question asks how offenders unable to respond or submit evidence would be handled fairly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: NEA will then fully review and consider the relevant circumstances of each case before taking any appropriate action against the owner(s)/tenant(s), which may include the issuance of a warning." I would like to ask if a possible offender does not have the ability to write in to NEA and hence does not respond to the notice of a fine in time and does not have relatives to assist, how would the case be handled, so as to give that person a fair hearing as regards to possible evidence of innocence that they might be able to share?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And lower-income owners may not have the time or resources to submit evidence to prove that they were not responsible for the high-rise littering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, my question is, will sufficient consideration be given to such factors if such individuals seek to appeal against a fine by providing some evidence against the presumption of guilt but they have missed the deadline, for these reasons?

sections.label: CCTV use and privacy concerns
sections.summary: The question asks whether owners might install CCTV cameras to rebut the presumption of guilt against tenants or domestic workers, raising privacy issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Or what if owners use this law as a reason to install CCTV cameras to make sure they have evidence to rebut the presumption of guilt vis-à-vis their tenants or domestic workers, which raises privacy issues?

sections.label: Doubled litter penalties
sections.summary: The Act was amended to double the maximum penalties for litter-related offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Act was also amended to double the maximum penalties for litter-related offences.

sections.label: Littering enforcement and feedback figures
sections.summary: Minister Grace Fu stated NEA enforced around 7,400 littering cases from January to May 2021, and before 2019 averaged 16,000 feedback cases yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Minister Grace Fu in a Parliamentary reply in July 2022 said "NEA carried out enforcement actions on around 7,400 cases of littering between 1 January to 31 May 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Prior to 2019, an average of 16,000 feedback cases were received each year.

sections.label: Support for presumption clause
sections.summary: The speaker supports clause 5 of the amendment Bill to insert a presumption clause to better identify the litter bug in the flat unit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Why have we deteriorated to such a situation today?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Hence, I support clause 5 of the current amendment Bill to insert a presumption clause to better identify the litter bug in the flat unit.

sections.label: Concerns over presumption of guilt
sections.summary: The speaker wants strong action on littering but is concerned that proposed section 17A presumes owners or tenants responsible unless they prove another person committed the act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Government should send a strong signal that littering is not to be tolerated and that stern action would be taken to ensure that all citizens would be able to enjoy a clean environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I look forward to the day when Singapore is able to reclaim its position as one of the cleanest cities in the region – not because of our army of cleaners, but because everyone in Singapore takes their social responsibility of keeping the public area clean seriously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: However, I do have some concerns with the new proposed section 17A which creates a presumption that the owners or tenants of the property are responsible if any refuse or article is deposited, dropped, placed, thrown, scattered or spilled in or into a public place from a residential flat, for the current section 17(1)(a), (d) and (f), unless they can prove that the act was committed by another person, that the owners or tenants were not present at the flat or they are able to provide the identity of the offender within 14 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While I can understand the intention of the authorities to make it easier for the enforcement, especially with the rising number of high-rise littering cases and the amendments may well help to make prosecution easier, I am concerned that the presumption of guilt on the part of owners or tenants may place these persons in a difficult position to clear themselves, even if they were not ultimately or directly responsible for the littering, spitting or disposing acts.

sections.label: Discretion not to prosecute
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether authorities will exercise discretion not to prosecute owners or tenants put in a difficult position by the new law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will the authorities exercise some form of discretion not to prosecute owners or tenants who might be put in a spot by the new law in the way that I have described?

sections.label: NEA cameras and enforcement actions
sections.summary: NEA deployed an average of 2,400 cameras annually and conducted about 1,500 enforcement actions annually against high-rise littering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Over the same time period, NEA has also deployed an average of 2,400 cameras annually and conducted about 1,500 enforcement actions annually against persons caught for high-rise littering.

sections.label: Understated high-rise littering complaints
sections.summary: The speaker views NEA's cited 30,000 complaints as much smaller than actual numbers because the public is resigned to the problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The number of high-rise litterers that was cited by NEA of 30,000 complaints, in my view, a much smaller number than we know of, as the majority of the public are resigned to the fact that these are the problems and we have to live with the problems.

sections.label: NEA surveillance and forensic capabilities
sections.summary: The speaker says NEA needs better high-rise surveillance equipment and stronger investigative capabilities, including forensic tools like DNA, as the Police possesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: NEA needs to invest in more and better high‐rise surveillance equipment and NEA also needs to build up stronger capabilities to investigate, including deploying forensic tools, such as DNA; the sort of capabilities that the Police possesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: As it involved a sad fatality, the Police took over the investigation and, within 10 days, the high-rise litterer was apprehended and prosecuted.

sections.label: NEA littering enforcement challenge
sections.summary: A speaker challenges NEA to take a litterer at Blk 203 to task within three months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Perhaps, I can throw this challenge to the NEA team to attend to this case at Blk 203; just one of the many cases that I have and demonstrate that with the means and capabilities that NEA has, the litterer can be taken to task in the next three months.

sections.label: Cleaning companies wage breaches
sections.summary: A 2021 report found 57 licensed cleaning companies did not pay eligible cleaners bonuses or progressive wages, and 52 firms were warned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A 2021 report revealed that 57 licensed cleaning companies did not pay eligible cleaners bonuses or progressive wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Another 52 firms were issued warnings for similar breaches.

sections.label: Class 1 and Class 2 licences
sections.summary: The revised framework differs significantly between Class 1 and Class 2 licences, with paid-up capital 10 times more for Class 1.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Furthermore, with regard to the revised framework, I understand that there is a significant difference in the requirements for Class 1 and Class 2 licences, specifically in terms of paid-up capital, which is 10 times more for Class 1.

sections.label: Littering by children elderly disabled
sections.summary: A speaker asks what percentage of littering cases are attributed to children, the elderly or individuals with certain disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To that end, I would like to know what percentage of littering cases are currently being attributed to children, the elderly or individuals with certain disabilities.

sections.label: High-rise littering complaints and penalties
sections.summary: High-rise littering complaints doubled between 2019 and 2021 versus 2016 to 2018, and the amendment aims to reduce proceedings costs and use public resources effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Complaints about high-rise littering have in fact doubled between 2019 and 2021 as compared to between 2016 to 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The proposed amendment is timely as this would reduce cost in proceedings against individuals who commit high-rise littering and allow for more effective use of public resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As we work to strengthen our enforcement efforts against littering, we should not forget the full range of penalties available to us, including the use of Corrective Work Orders (CWOs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While fines may be an effective deterrent for some, they may not always have the desired impact for those who can afford to pay the fines without feeling the pinch.

sections.label: Owners maintaining waste systems
sections.summary: All owners, including strata owners, must ensure waste systems function properly, and the speaker supports the Bill empowering the Director-General to enforce against owners who fail to maintain, repair and replace systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is the responsibility of all owners, including strata owners, to ensure that the systems are functioning properly to move waste efficiently to keep the building and surrounding environment clean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I support the new Bill's proposals that empower the Director-General to take enforcement actions against property owners who fail to maintain, repair and replace their systems.

sections.label: Penalties for littering and feeding birds
sections.summary: Asks whether the new Bill penalises feeding birds and whether NEA can penalise those leaving rubbish, renovation debris and cardboards in common areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Will the new Bill penalise those who throw food to feed birds?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Could NEA also investigate and penalise those who have left rubbish along public corridors and in common areas, since there are often their address or other identifiable markings left on the rubbish?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Can NEA also punish those irresponsible contractors and home owners who dispose of their renovation debris and packing cardboards downstairs?

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model for waste management
sections.summary: The waste management PWM raises baseline wages over six years from 2023 to 2028, with entry-level pay growing 8.1% annually from $2,210 to $3,260, plus overtime and bonuses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The PWM for the waste management industry will increase baseline wages in a sustained manner over a six-year period from 2023 to 2028.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Entry-level wage for waste collection crew will grow 8.1% annually from $2,210 in 2023 to $3,260 in 2028.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: They will also enjoy overtime payments and mandatory annual bonuses.

sections.label: Transitional wage support for companies
sections.summary: Companies can tap transitional wage support under MOM's Progressive Wage Credit Scheme to ease the cost increase.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To ease the cost increase, the companies can tap on transitional wage support that is provided under MOM’s Progressive Wage Credit Scheme.

sections.label: Monthly waste collection fees
sections.summary: Monthly waste collection fees are $9.72 for HDB flats and condominiums based on household units and $32.37 for landed housing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Currently, the monthly waste collection fees are set at $9.72 for HDB flats and condominiums based on household units and $32.37 for landed housing.

sections.label: Solid waste generated and recycled
sections.summary: In 2021, close to seven million tonnes of solid waste were generated and about 55% was recycled.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2021, close to seven million tonnes of solid waste were generated and about 55% was recycled.

sections.label: Technology, design and fee structure
sections.summary: Besides growing the PWM crew pool, better design, technology and work processes are needed to automate waste collection, and a fairer fee structure to support cost increase.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Other than growing the pool of waste management crew with the PWM, we will need to leverage better design and technology and improve work processes to automate the waste collection process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We also need to look at a fairer waste collection fee structure to support the cost increase.

sections.label: High-rise littering and cleaning licensing
sections.summary: The speech covers mandatory education for high-rise littering re-offenders, cleaning licensing costs, and uplifting waste workers, noting complaints rose to 32,000 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My speech will focus on three considerations related to the Bill: one, suggestion for mandatory education or counselling for re-offenders of high-rise littering; two, cost considerations for the proposed revision in the cleaning business licensing framework; and three, creating a conducive environment to uplift workers of waste collection and waste disposal services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I recall in October last year, Minister Grace Fu shared in this House that the number of complaints about high-rise littering had almost doubled from an average of 16,000 annually before 2016 to 32,000 cases in 2021.

sections.label: High-rise cigarette butt offences
sections.summary: Between 2019 and 2022, 54% of NEA-enforced high-rise littering offences were for cigarette butts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Between 2019 and 2022, 54% of total high-rise littering offences enforced by NEA were for high-rise cigarette butt littering.

sections.label: Littering fines under amendment Bill
sections.summary: The amendment Bill makes littering offenders liable to Court fines of up to $2,000 for a first conviction and $4,000 to $10,000 for later convictions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Currently, under the amendment Bill, individuals who commit a littering offence is liable on conviction to a Court fine of up to $2,000 for a first conviction and higher amounts of $4,000 to $10,000 on second and subsequent convictions.

sections.label: Regulations for PWM implementation
sections.summary: New proposed sections 23A(2) and 31AA(2) enable regulations requiring waste collector and waste disposal licensees to implement the PWM for their workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Lastly, the new proposed sections 23A(2) and 31AA(2) are introduced to enable regulations to be made to require waste collector and waste disposal licensees to implement the PWM for their workers.

sections.label: Waste management licensing framework amendment
sections.summary: The Government will amend the waste management licensing framework to encourage higher wages and ensure funds for worker training and productivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Second, I understand that the Government will amend the waste management licensing framework to encourage businesses to raise wages at all levels to help attract and retain workers, and to ensure that they have sufficient funds to train workers to raise their productivity.

sections.label: PWM for waste management operators
sections.summary: The licensing framework amendment prepares waste management operators for the Progressive Wage Model from July 2023, benefiting about 3,000 local workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Third, I also support the Government's move to amend the licensing framework for waste management operators to prepare them for the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) to be implemented from July 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The implementation of PWM will benefit about 3,000 local workers.

sections.label: Support for waste workers PWM
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill and welcomes the Progressive Wage Model for waste collection and disposal workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my considerations raised, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, I welcome the introduction of the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) for waste collection and disposal workers.

sections.label: Littering enforcement and fines
sections.summary: The clause presumes the registered owner or tenant is the offender, with fines starting at $2,000 for the first offence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The proposed clause would make it easier for NEA to take enforcement action against littering from residential flats by automatically presuming the registered owner or tenant is the offender.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The proposed fines, starting at $2,000 for the first offence and increasing with subsequent convictions, will serve as a strong deterrent against littering.

sections.label: Extending 14-day period
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry could consider extending the period of 14 days to 30 days.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry consider extending the period of 14 days to 30 days?

sections.label: High-rise littering complaints doubled
sections.summary: High-rise littering complaints rose to an average of 29,700 between 2019 and 2021, with offenders unidentified in about 15% of cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Complaints in Singapore about high-rise littering have almost doubled to an average of 29,700 between 2019 and 2021, as compared to an average of 16,800 between 2016 and 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Given that the offender typically could not be identified in about 15% of cases investigated from 2019 to 2021, I am hopeful that the amendment would lead to residents taking stronger ownership in preventing such acts from their homes.

sections.label: Waste sector wage increase questions
sections.summary: About 3,000 Singaporeans and PRs work in waste management, and the speaker asks who bears the wage increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: With about 3,000 Singaporeans and Permanent Residents (PRs) working in the waste management sector, the increase in their wages over the next six years under the PWM is timely and welcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: How much of the pay increase is likely to be subsidised by the Government or absorbed by the employers or would the industry players be likely to transfer the bulk of the wage increase to the end consumers?

sections.label: Complaints doubled, enforcement stagnated
sections.summary: Complaints doubled in recent years while enforcement actions stagnated at around 1,500 instances annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The number of complaints has doubled in recent years, but enforcement actions has stagnated at around 1,500 instances annually.

sections.label: Littering fine range
sections.summary: A person is liable to a fine ranging from $2,000 to $10,000 for littering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Currently, a person is liable to a fine ranging from $2,000 to $10,000 for littering.

sections.label: OBC adoption by service buyers
sections.summary: OBCs are adopted by all Government service buyers and 40% of large industry service buyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: OBCs are now adopted by all Government service buyers and 40% of large service buyers in the industry.

sections.label: Waste management PWM timing
sections.summary: The PWM in the waste management industry will take effect later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The PWM in the waste management industry will take effect later this year.

sections.label: Speaker support for Bill
sections.summary: The Speaker states that notwithstanding the suggestions, he supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the suggestions, Speaker, Sir, I support the Bill.

sections.label: NEA littering complaints numbers
sections.summary: NEA received 22,000 complaints in 2019, 35,000 in 2020 and 32,000 in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: From 22,000 complaints received by NEA in 2019, 2020 and 2021 saw NEA receiving 35,000 and 32,000 complaints respectively.

sections.label: High-rise littering enforcement and burden of proof
sections.summary: About 1,500 annual enforcement actions were taken from 2017 to 2021 against high-rise littering, with about 25,000 average complaints; the amendment shifts the burden of proof to flat owners and occupiers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Based on reported averages, approximately 1,500 enforcement actions were taken annually between 2017 and 2021 for high-rise littering, while NEA received an average of about 25,000 such complaints during the same period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The stark differences between the number of enforcement actions taken against high-rise littering versus the number of complaints received further drive home the point that it is never easy to take actions against those who engage in such behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe the amendment to shift the burden of proof from NEA having to prove that a particular individual in the flat has littered, to the flat owners and occupiers proving that they did not litter is a step in the right direction in ensuring greater efficiency in tackling the scourge of high-rise littering.

sections.label: Fatal killer litter incident
sections.summary: A wine bottle thrown from a condominium unit struck and killed a 73-year-old man.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the same year, a wine bottle was thrown out of a condominium unit, striking a 73-year-old man, resulting in his death.

sections.label: Corrective Work Orders for littering
sections.summary: Corrective Work Orders, introduced in 1992, numbered about 10,200 from 2017 to 2021 and aim to change offenders' behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I think this was touched on by hon Members Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Lim Biow Chuan regarding the matter of Corrective Work Orders (CWOs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: They were first introduced in 1992 for offenders of littering to increase offenders’ awareness of the impact of littering, as well as for them to experience the difficulties faced by cleaners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: From 2017 to 2021, a total of approximately 10,200 CWOs were issued, making up a small percentage of the total number of tickets issued during that period for littering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As painful as a fine can be, there are those who might be financially comfortable enough to pay off the fine and the fine has no material or any sort of impact on them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, performing CWOs would allow them to empathise with the cleaners and realise how their inconsiderate behaviour has impacted others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I think this is likely to be more impactful in bringing about a behavioural change instead of the issuance of a fine.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am especially heartened to note the implementation of the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) for waste management and materials recovery workers starting 1 July 2023, which aims to boost the salaries of about 3,000 resident workers.

sections.label: Cleaning business licence requirements
sections.summary: Only one-third of 1,550 licensed cleaning businesses qualify for renewable Class 2 licences requiring $25,000 paid-up capital.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the long run, cleaning businesses are expected to hold the renewable Class 2 licences which require licensees to hold a paid-up capital of at least $25,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, in January 2023, it was observed that only one-third of the 1,550 licensed cleaning businesses currently qualify for this licence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While NEA has provided that the start date of this new framework will only take place in 2024, does NEA foresee any shocks to the industry, should a large number of companies be unable to keep their licences and provide cleaning services?

sections.label: Killer litter and flat owners
sections.summary: About 15% of killer litter culprits are never identified, and the new law could place greater onus on flat owners and tenants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In my constituency too, unfortunately, despite repeated advisories, public education and more intensive clean-ups, we do see such behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And given that about 15% of killer litter culprits are never identified, the new law could place greater onus on flat owners and tenants serving as a possible deterrent.

sections.label: Complex cases and Bill measures
sections.summary: The Bill aims to boost public cleanliness and hygiene and increase authorities' ability to act swiftly and effectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Could NEA please share what are some examples of such complex cases and based on complaints in the last three years, could NEA provide an indication of the proportion of cases that would benefit from being extended from beyond a year?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In closing, this Bill underscores the Government's commitment to boosting public cleanliness and hygiene.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The proposed measures increase the authorities' ability to act swiftly and effectively while guiding companies towards greater professionalism.

sections.label: Referral to mental health institute
sections.summary: The question asks whether NEA can immediately refer alleged culprits to the Institute of Mental Health for swift medical assessments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can NEA refer these alleged culprits to the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) immediately, so that the medical assessments can be made swiftly?

sections.label: NEA referral to IMH
sections.summary: A question asks whether NEA can be empowered to refer offenders to IMH for assessments directly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Is it possible to empower NEA to refer them to IMH for assessments directly?

sections.label: Minimum time between fines
sections.summary: A question asks whether a minimum time period applies before second and third fines are issued to recalcitrant offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For recalcitrant offenders, is there a minimum time period when they will be issued the second and third fines after they have committed the first and second offences respectively?

sections.label: Town Councils installing CCTVs
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Bill allows Town Councils to install CCTVs to catch suspects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can this Bill allow Town Councils to install CCTVs to catch the suspects?

sections.label: PWM for waste workers
sections.summary: The PWM is introduced to support resident waste management workers through skills, wages, job prospects and career progression.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Several Members have spoken in support of the need to uplift our lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We are introducing the PWM to support our resident waste management workers by improving their skills, uplifting their wages and offering better job prospects and career progression.

sections.label: Wage schedule and mid-term review
sections.summary: The multi-year wage schedule from 2023 to 2028 gives industry certainty, with a mid-term review in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To Dr Wan Rizal's suggestion to compress the wage schedule, the multi-year wage schedule from 2023 to 2028 has been set out to provide greater certainty to the industry so that they can plan for the changes in determining the wage recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To ensure the wage schedule remains relevant, a mid-term review would be undertaken in 2025.

sections.label: Cleaning sector PWM penalties
sections.summary: Penalties in 2021 and 2022 stayed stable, averaging about five financial penalties and 30 warning letters yearly to cleaning licensees.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: On Mr Yip Hon Weng's question on the enforcement of PWM requirements for the cleaning sector, the number of penalties imposed in 2021 and 2022 has remained stable, where an average of about five financial penalties have been imposed on and 30 warning letters have been issued to cleaning business licensees each year.

sections.label: Cleaning business licence classes
sections.summary: Cleaning businesses must attain Class 1 or 2 licences after two years, while those not meeting requirements can apply for Class 3 with two more years to transit.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: At a steady state, all cleaning businesses will have to attain Class 1 or 2 licences after two years of joining the industry and will have to ensure skills training and workplace safety for their workforce and attain corresponding levels of financial ability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Existing cleaning business licensees, including new entrants that do not meet the requirements for the Class 1 or Class 2 licence can apply for the Class 3 licence and have an additional two years to grow their capabilities and transit to the Class 1 or Class 2 licences.

sections.label: Government procuring entities Class 1 licence
sections.summary: NEA is working with MOF towards requiring Government Procuring Entities to engage only cleaning businesses with a Class 1 licence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Additionally, NEA is working with the Ministry of Finance (MOF) towards requiring Government Procuring Entities to engage only cleaning businesses with a Class 1 licence.

sections.label: Consultation and revised framework start date
sections.summary: NEA consulted the cleaning industry and considered feedback, so the revised framework only comes into effect on 1 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Prior to revising the framework, NEA had consulted the cleaning industry extensively and considered specific feedback on the new requirements for the Class 1 and 2 licences.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We also factored in the request for more time to transit and therefore planned for the revised framework to only come into effect on 1 January 2024.

sections.label: Presumptions exclude common corridors littering
sections.summary: The presumptions will not cover littering from common corridors and staircases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The presumptions will not cover littering from common corridors and staircases.

sections.label: Surveillance cameras and high-rise littering
sections.summary: NEA increased surveillance camera deployments by over 50% in 2020 and deploys about 200 monthly, with high-rise littering captured in about 35% of deployments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: NEA had increased the number of surveillance camera deployments by over 50% in 2020 and currently deploys about 200 surveillance cameras each month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: High-rise littering incidences are captured in about 35% of such camera deployments, on average, over a five-year period.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In 2020 and 2021, about 7% of high-rise littering cases were attributed to persons below the age of 19 and 24% to those above the age of 64.

sections.label: Penalties for high-rise littering offenders
sections.summary: Littering offenders can be fined up to $2,000, $4,000 and $10,000 for first, second and subsequent offences, with about 4% repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Several Members, including Mr Lim Biow Chuan, asked if current penalties were effective, particularly against recalcitrant offenders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We have stiff penalties for high-rise littering and only about 4% of offenders who litter from residential flats are repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Littering offenders can be fined up to $2,000, $4,000 and $10,000 for their first, second and subsequent offences respectively.

sections.label: Terminating leases of recalcitrant offenders
sections.summary: The suggestion to terminate leases of recalcitrant flat owners is a harsh measure not to be undertaken lightly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The suggestion to terminate the lease of flat owners who are recalcitrant offenders is a harsh measure that ought not to be undertaken lightly.

sections.label: Town Councils maintaining PWCS
sections.summary: Town Councils are required under the Town Councils Act to maintain, repair and replace the PWCS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To Mr Don Wee’s question on what can be done to address errant acts that result in blockages of the PWCS, Town Councils are required under the Town Councils Act to maintain, repair and replace the PWCS.

sections.label: PWCS costs and section 20 prohibition
sections.summary: PWCS capital and maintenance costs are small proportions, with savings expected from reduced manpower, and section 20 prohibits vehicle dumping in public places.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Based on our consultations, the additional capital cost of PWCS is a small proportion of the total cost of a development and the maintenance cost is also a small proportion of the building's operational costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With the increasing manpower challenges and the rising cost of labour, we can expect more cost savings due to the reduced manpower requirement of PWCS, not to mention the environmental benefits from the reduction in pest infestation, odours and exposed waste.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: To clarify, the prohibition in section 20 applies to the use of a vehicle to dump waste in a public place or the dumping of waste from a vehicle in a public place.

sections.label: Extension of EPHA limitation period
sections.summary: The extended limitation period in section 95 applies to any EPHA offence except one involving injury or danger to health subsisting at complaint date.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: With regard to the extension of the limitation period in section 95 of the Act, I would like to clarify that this would apply to any offence committed under the EPHA, other than an offence that involves an injury or danger to health that subsists at the date of the complaint of the offence, and not only illegal dumping cases.

sections.label: Catch rate figure
sections.summary: The catch rate is 35%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: You will see that, as I have shared, the catch rate is 35%.

sections.label: Repeat offenders percentage unknown
sections.summary: The percentage of repeat offenders is not available, but it is a minority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: So, the number of repeat offenders – what is the percentage?

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I do not have the numbers here, but it is a minority.

sections.label: Court discretion and fines as deterrent
sections.summary: Courts may issue a CWO at their discretion, but low repeat-offender numbers show fines deter, so CWOs are not necessary even for first-time offenders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: In fact, it is at the discretion of the Courts to issue a CWO, where they think it is fit to do so.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But having said that, we are saying that fines are actually effective as a deterrent because based on our statistics, of those who have been caught and had been enforced against, the number of repeat offenders is very low.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Hence, we think that it is not necessary, even for first-time offenders, to be issued a CWO by the Court.
